# Kyoto 4-Day Slow-Travel Plan

A calm Kyoto trip works best with one anchor sight per day, short transit hops, and neighborhood-based dinners. I’ve kept this plan within a **$1,800 total budget for 2 adults, excluding flights**, with a comfortable mid-range pace.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Cost Plan

| Day | Main focus | Morning | Afternoon | Evening | Est. cost for 2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---:|
| Apr 10 | Higashiyama + Kiyomizu-dera | Arrive, check in, easy lunch near Gion | **Kiyomizu-dera** and nearby lanes | Gion stroll + tea house or river walk | **$310** |
| Apr 11 | Arashiyama | Slow breakfast, scenic train/bus ride west | **Tenryu-ji** garden and bamboo grove area | Dinner in Arashiyama or central Kyoto | **$285** |
| Apr 12 | Central Kyoto + market day | **Nishiki Market** tasting walk | Rest, cafe stop, optional shopping | Pontocho alley dinner + casual nightlife | **$300** |
| Apr 13 | Northern Kyoto | Check out, light luggage drop if needed | **Kinkaku-ji** and surrounding garden time | Early farewell dinner / departure prep | **$260** |

## Sample Slow-Pace Itinerary

### Day 1: Higashiyama Arrival
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Arrive in Kyoto, check into a central hotel, and keep the first half-day light.
- Afternoon: Visit **Kiyomizu-dera** as your main temple of the day, then wander Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka at an easy pace.
- Food: Simple lunch or early dinner in Gion/Higashiyama; choose set meals or soba to keep costs controlled.
- Evening: Take a relaxed walk along the **Kamo River** or through Gion’s lantern-lit streets.

### Day 2: Arashiyama Garden Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Head west after breakfast and keep transit unhurried.
- Afternoon: Make **Tenryu-ji** your only major stop, then enjoy the garden and bamboo area without rushing.
- Food: Lunch near Arashiyama station or a casual tofu/soba spot.
- Evening: Return to central Kyoto for a quiet dinner; optional short walk around Kyoto Station area.

### Day 3: Market and Evening Scene
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- Morning: Visit **Nishiki Market** for a tasting-focused food walk; go early for the best pace and fewer crowds.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Morning: Visit **Nishiki Market** for a tasting-focused food walk; go early for the best pace and fewer crowds, Kyoto, Japan
- Afternoon: Rest at a cafe, browse Teramachi or Shinkyogoku, and keep the rest of the day flexible.
- Food: Use the market visit as your main lunch; share small bites to stay on budget.
Media: Alt=Food: Use the market visit as your main lunch; share small bites to stay on budget, Kyoto, Japan
- Evening: Dinner in **Pontocho** or along the Kamo River, then a gentle nightlife stroll.

### Day 4: Northern Kyoto Farewell
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/sun.svg
- Morning: Check out and store luggage if needed.
- Afternoon: Visit **Kinkaku-ji** as the day’s single headline sight, then leave time for a calm return.
- Food: Light lunch near the site or back in central Kyoto before departure.
- Evening: Early farewell dinner or train/airport transfer prep.

## Budget Fit for 2 Adults

- Lodging: **$900–$1,100** for 3 nights in a clean mid-range hotel or apartment
- Food: **$260–$360** total
- Local transit: **$50–$90** total
- Entry fees and small extras: **$80–$140** total
- Buffer for snacks, coffee, and flexibility: **$100–$180**

This keeps the trip comfortably near **$1,800 total** if you choose smart lodging and avoid expensive fine dining.

## Best Neighborhoods to Stay In

### 1) Kyoto Station area
- Best for: transport convenience, easy arrivals/departures, straightforward budgeting
- Good fit if: you want the simplest logistics and reliable hotel value
- Trade-off: less atmospheric than Gion or Higashiyama

### 2) Kawaramachi / Shijo
- Best for: central location, restaurants, shopping, easy evening walks
- Good fit if: you want balance between convenience and atmosphere
- Trade-off: can cost a bit more than Kyoto Station

### 3) Gion / Higashiyama edge
- Best for: traditional Kyoto feel, walkable access to temples and evening scenery
- Good fit if: you want the most classic trip experience
- Trade-off: hotel prices can rise quickly, so prioritize smaller inns or business hotels nearby

### 4) Karasuma / Oike
- Best for: quieter central base, good subway access, solid mid-range pricing
- Good fit if: you want calm evenings and easy movement across the city
- Trade-off: fewer postcard-style streets right outside your door
